record.confidence_note: the Buddy pricing page, plans-and-features doc, usage doc, signup page, API overview and pipeline UI doc were read and quoted on 2026-11-19; no pipeline was run, so the CPU, memory and disk of a pipeline run and the exact build log retention period are unverified

free_tier.stated: Free plan at EUR 0: 1 seat, 2 concurrents, USD 1 of usage credit per month for compute and storage, and 1 GB of pipeline cache; all features except SSO and advanced permissions
free_tier.notes: the USD 1 credit buys CPU-minutes, GB-minutes and GB-hours at the published rates, so the free allowance is a dollar budget rather than a fixed minute count; 1 GB of pipeline cache is included on top

per_object_cap.stated: no per-object cap stated; the free plan includes 1 GB of pipeline cache

retention.stated: a free workspace with no login is frozen after 60 days and permanently terminated if no action is taken in the following 30 days; pipeline runs alone do not count as activity
retention.notes: the 90 days is the sum of the 60-day inactivity window and the following 30 days before permanent termination: 60 + 30 = 90

egress.terms: no egress allowance or per-GB price is published; storage is billed per GB-hour at USD 0.00011 for sandbox and artifact storage and USD 0.00068 for the pipeline cache

record.interface_detail: the REST API is described by an OpenAPI 3 specification and is reached at api.buddy.works, api.eu.buddy.works or api.asia.buddy.works with an OAuth2 bearer token; pipelines are defined in the web editor, in YAML or imported from YAML, and the bdy CLI starts and follows pipeline runs
record.tooling: a browser-based visual pipeline builder, YAML pipeline definitions, the bdy CLI and a REST API with an OpenAPI 3 specification; pipelines run in containers or Linux, Windows and macOS VMs with x64 or ARM64 CPUs; self-hosted Buddy installations exist but are software the reader installs and runs and come after this hosted offer
record.chaining: a Git push, pull request, schedule or webhook starts a pipeline; containers make up over 90% of actions and consume the USD 1 monthly credit at USD 0.00024 per CPU-minute and GB-minute, with higher GB-minute multipliers for Windows and macOS; a free pipeline stops once the credit is used up and resumes when it renews

limits.value: USD 1 of usage credit per month on Free, spent on CPU-minutes, GB-minutes and GB-hours; no pay-as-you-go billing on Free
2 concurrent pipeline runs on Free, a hard limit with no extra concurrents sold
1 seat and 1 GB of pipeline cache on Free
a free workspace is frozen after 60 days with no login and permanently terminated if no action is taken in the following 30 days

record.limits_note: the USD 1 credit buys 4,166 CPU-minutes or GB-minutes at the container rate of USD 0.00024 each: USD 1 / USD 0.00024 = 4,166.67; a macOS VM runs at USD 0.00144 per GB-minute, about six times faster; storage at USD 0.00011 per GB-hour also draws from the same credit
record.binding_note: the USD 1 monthly credit binds first: a free pipeline stops when the credit is used up and cannot be extended with pay-as-you-go, before 2 concurrent runs or the 60-day inactivity window matter

identity_cost.detail: the signup page offers GitHub, GitLab, Google or Bitbucket sign-in, or a work email address, full name and a password of at least 15 characters or 7 including a number; no phone number or card is asked for on that page, and the pricing page states 'No credit card required'

record.reliability_note: unverified: no suspension or data-loss event is stated on the pages read; a free workspace is frozen after 60 days without a login and terminated 30 days later, and pipelines and sandboxes stop when the monthly credit runs out

record.notes: Buddy's hosted CI/CD service is the subject of this record. A separate record, compute/buddy, holds the Buddy Sandboxes container and VM sandbox offer under the compute topic, and a domain-collision open question is filed. The free USD 1 monthly credit buys a variable number of minutes depending on the action type, so the allowance is a budget rather than a fixed minute count. Self-hosted Buddy installations are software the reader installs and runs, listed after this hosted offer.
